reason: S1 introduces the public per-parser-context error-callback API xmlCtxtSetErrorHandler and routes normal and out-of-memory parser errors through xmlParserCtxt.errorHandler/errorCtxt, including propagation to nested contexts. H0 only supplies shared fuzz-data, entity-loader, and allocation-failure helpers; it never creates a parser context, registers this handler, triggers parsing, or verifies callback routing and propagation. Thus the new callback protocol and its state transitions are not exercised.
evidence: include/libxml/parser.h adds xmlStructuredErrorFunc errorHandler and void *errorCtxt to xmlParserCtxt and publicly declares xmlCtxtSetErrorHandler.
parserInternals.c implements xmlCtxtSetErrorHandler by storing handler and data in ctxt->errorHandler and ctxt->errorCtxt.
xmlCtxtErrMemory and xmlVErrParser prioritize ctxt->errorHandler over ctxt->sax->serror and generic SAX error callbacks.
xmlParseBalancedChunkMemoryInternal and xmlCreateEntityParserCtxtInternal copy the registered handler into newly created nested parser contexts with xmlCtxtSetErrorHandler.

H0's xmlFuzzErrorFunc only discards generic errors, while xmlFuzzMemSetLimit and xmlFuzzMalloc provide failure injection; H0 contains no call to xmlCtxtSetErrorHandler or any parser entry point that could exercise the new callback behavior.
recommended_action: Add a harness entry point that creates an XML parser context, registers a structured callback with xmlCtxtSetErrorHandler using fuzz-controlled callback data, parses malformed and entity-bearing input, and combines allocation-failure injection with nested entity parsing to check callback delivery, context identity, propagation, and cleanup.
